tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. 2	name: connection-skill-per-connection-type
3	description: "2026-11-02 Kenneth's chosen proposal for how the agent gets better printer knowledge over time: one connection skill per connection type, added when a person connects, driven by honest tool states, grown by reviewed PRs and opt-in reports. Recorded, not implemented."
4	metadata:
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 73de5d33-07b2-44a6-bbd2-bedca734a244
8	  modified: 2026-11-02T13:35:27.756Z
9	---
10	
11	Kenneth confirmed this on 2026-11-02 (in a forked side session, "AI agent design for printer setup") as the one to try for the open problem in the P1S handoff: how the agent gets correct printer and connection knowledge when the team cannot test most printers. Nothing is implemented or scheduled.
12	
13	1. **When:** the moment a person tries to connect a printer in the chat, the app adds one skill to that conversation. Not before, and not for people who only pick a profile and prepare prints.
14	2. **What:** a text file in the repo, one per connection type (Bambu first, then Moonraker/OctoPrint), chosen by the app from the connection type, never by the model. It holds the procedure: which tool to call, what each reported state means, and the one right next step for each, including silence, where it tells the model to ask what the person sees and wait rather than conclude. It holds no menu wording the app cannot verify.
15	3. **Tools:** the status and connect tools report the situation exactly as the app observes it (heard nothing yet, port taken, plug-in missing, cloud mode, wrong code, the host's own refusal reason). The skill drives the conversation from those states; the tools never carry the procedure.
16	4. **Improvement loop:** the skill grows by pull request reviewed by a person, like OrcaSlicer's profiles. When the agent and the person are struggling, by a rule the app applies (a connect attempt failed twice, or the person corrected the model), the chat asks whether to send a report to the JusPrin developers. The person sees what will be sent and says yes or no; nothing is sent otherwise. The report holds the tool states and the connection turns, never the access code or API key, and goes to our server directly so people on their own API keys can send it too.
17	5. **Evidence rule:** before any skill line is written for a state, that state must have been made to happen for real. The Bambu side has mostly done this; the host side only for Moonraker and OctoPrint.
18	
19	**Why:** it replaces three earlier ideas Kenneth rejected: steps in the standing prompt, a "file per printer model" that was invented jargon and the wrong key for Klipper hosts, and counting data points, which OrcaSlicer never does. Connection type is the key the code already has.
20	
21	**How to apply:** when work on printer-connection guidance starts, build this, not a variant; check each state against [[p1s-connect-incident-2026-10-31]] and [[tool-result-states-method]] (Kenneth's test for what counts as a problem). Open as of 2026-11-02: Bambu plug-in code -1 on a wrong access code, never 5; whether -1 is a rejection or a timeout.

3	description: "2026-11-01/02 tool-result sweep: Kenneth's test for a result bug (a person stuck: told something false, right step hidden, cost beyond one call); how the problem statement drifted into 'every distinguishable state' and eight of nine fixes were taken out; branch claude/tool-results-truth"
4	metadata:

10	
11	After the P1S cloud-mode incident (2026-10-31) a code-reading sweep listed eleven tools whose result said less than the app knew, and I fixed nine of them on `claude/tool-silent-failures` (common branch `claude/tool-results-truth`). On 2026-11-02 Kenneth asked why, and eight came out again.
12	
13	**Kenneth's test for a tool-result bug:** a person who plausibly exists, told something false or useless at that moment, with the right next step hidden, at a cost beyond one more tool call. "Fixing a non-problem is a lot worse than not fixing a real problem." The model recovering the truth with its next ordinary call is not a stuck person. The three that passed: a wrong Bambu access code read as a vanished printer; a print host that answered read as unreachable; a heard printer hidden from the connection (same loop as the incident).
14	
15	**How the statement drifted:** incident (a person stuck, false reason, right step hidden) → sweep ("a tool says less than the app knew", a code shape, eleven matches by reading) → brief ("a class of bug", method + guard, "reproduce before fixing") → my reading (reproduce = make two states read the same over MCP, a property of the code). Each hand-off made it easier to satisfy. The hidden-preset "fix" was the clearest non-problem: no person, the sweep itself said "may be intended".
16	
17	**Why:** the P1S failure was real because you were on the wrong side of it for an evening; the other ten shared its code shape, not its substance. Every field added for a non-problem is text every model reads on every call.
18	
19	**How to apply:** before fixing a result, write the scenario in Kenneth's terms (who, doing what, told what, losing what, which step is hidden); if it cannot be written, it is not a problem, whatever the code looks like. When a brief says "reproduce", ask whether it means "find the case a person hit" (it does, [[reproduce-on-real-app-not-fakes]]) before accepting a weaker reading, and raise the gap on receipt, not when asked three times. A rule or guard is worth keeping when it would fail on the real incident; a document nobody reads is not ([[rare-failures-get-a-generic-error]] still stands). Kept guards: `test_printer_conversation.cpp` "reports every printer it heard", harness `*_are_told_apart`, `FakeBambuAgent::fail_next_connect`, `StandInHost(hold, answer, status, body)`. Seam: one line in `GUI_App.cpp`'s local-connect CallAfter → `Printers::record_connection_event`; upstream/main added a log line at the same spot, resolve by keeping both.
20

10	
11	Added 2026-11-01 in ff2fee4fbd on claude/festive-lederberg-693438 (unmerged). `printer_connect` and `printer_connection_status` have only `ToolExposure::Printer`, so MCP answers "This tool is not exposed by JusPrin MCP", despite what [[manual-mcp-tool-repro-recipe]] implies for "any tool".
12	
13	`JusPrinShellHarness --printer-network-check <dir> <address> <plugin-version> [--simulate-announce]`: copy `plugins/` from the real data folder into `<dir>` first. Without the flag it needs a P1S in cloud mode on; with it, the harness replays the logged announcement into `DeviceManager::on_machine_alive` at 25 s, which tests everything after the plug-in.
14	
15	Another running JusPrin holding UDP 2021 hides the printer (2026-11-01, same P1S: nothing in 120 s with it running, found in 8 s with it quit), so quit it first (`lsof -nP -iUDP:2021`). Bambu Studio and OrcaSlicer not tried.
16	
17	The plug-in's `start_discovery` returns success even when the port is held, and it binds UDP 2021 only as the app starts: after the holder lets go, stop + start (with waits, with the sending flag) and `hot_reload_network_plugin()` all left the port empty on 2026-11-01. So the app reports `port_taken` / `not_listening` and asks for a restart; do not retry a recovery without a new idea. Hold the port from a Python socket to test those states.
18	
19	TCP 8883 is no test of whether a P1S is on: it timed out while the printer was announcing on UDP. To test, bind UDP 2021 and listen; announcements came within seconds.
20	
21	LAN mode, 2026-11-01: on the same P1S, LAN Only changes the announcement to `DevConnect: lan`, `DevBind: free`. The committed check fails there because it expects cloud mode; those runs used a temporary script. Whether a run starts before the printer is heard depends on the announcement timing (about every 20 s), so check the first "heard" line. A status read that lists the printer suppresses the note by design, so leave it out when testing the note.
22	
23	Wrong access code, 2026-11-02, P1S firmware 01.10.00.00 in LAN mode, plug-in 02.03.00.62: a connection with a wrong 8-character code made the plug-in answer `ConnectStatusFailed` with msg `-1`, twice, not the `5` upstream's handler treats as a wrong password. So the erase did not run and the wrong code stayed saved. Whether `-1` means the printer refused the code is not known: the plug-in's own log is encrypted (`debug_network_*.log.enc`), TCP 8883 and 990 did accept connections from the same Mac, and a run with the real code has not been done to compare. `5` has never been seen on real hardware.

1	# Bambu connection fixes: what was checked, 2026-11-01
2	
3	Temporary note, untracked. Three bugs in the printer chat's connection tools are fixed on branch
4	`claude/festive-lederberg-693438` (commit `ff2fee4fbd`), and the check against the real P1S passes. A later commit reports another app holding the port.
5	
6	## Wrong access code and the same printer saved twice, real P1S, 2026-11-02 04:58 to 05:23
7	
8	Real P1S at 192.168.0.198 in LAN mode (`lan`, `free`, firmware 01.10.00.00), real plug-in 02.03.00.62, real panel, a
9	temporary script instead of a model. Before is `ff10faa501`; after is `788ff792b7`. One attempt per version with the
10	deliberately wrong code `WRONG123`. A temporary line printed the plug-in's answer, because the app log does not.
11	
12	Entry B of the same model, unlinked, with entry A linked by writing the serial into the link record:
13	
14	```
15	before: printer_connection_status -> candidates: [], seen: []
16	before: note: The network search has listened for 15 seconds and has found no printer of this model.
17	before: printer_connect -> The network search has listened for 25 seconds and has found no printer of this model in LAN mode.
18	after:  printer_connection_status -> seen: [{"address":"192.168.0.198","detail":"Bambu Lab P1S","name":"P1s","reason":"linked_elsewhere"}]
19	after:  printer_connect -> P1s at 192.168.0.198 was seen on the network, but it is already the printer "Bambu Lab P1S" in this app, and a device connects to one saved printer. It cannot be connected as it is.
20	```
21	
22	Wrong code on entry A:
23	
24	```
25	both:   plug-in answered: state=1 (failed) msg=-1
26	both:   a modal dialog appeared; the script closed it. In this path its text is "Connect P1s failed! [SN:..., code=-1]"
27	both:   saved access code after the attempt: in memory present, in app config present
28	before: Connection to Bambu Lab P1S failed: The selected printer changed. Select this printer again to reconnect.
29	after:  Connection to Bambu Lab P1S failed: The printer refused the connection; Bambu's network plug-in reported code -1. Check that the printer is on and in LAN mode, then try again.
30	```
31	
32	What did not match the assumptions:
33	
34	- The plug-in said `-1`, not `5`. `5` has never been seen on real hardware.
35	- The before text was "The selected printer changed", not "The printer is no longer available".
36	- The wrong code was not erased, because the erase runs only on `5`. The code from the attempt stayed saved.
37	- The app log has no line with the code. The plug-in's own log is encrypted (`debug_network_*.log.enc`).
38	
39	Not known: whether `-1` means the printer refused the code. The app log shows 22 seconds between selecting the printer
40	(05:22:46.16) and the failure clearing it (05:23:08.25). My guess is that this is a timeout and not a refusal, but nothing
41	confirms it. TCP 8883 and 990 accepted connections from the same Mac. The after text says "refused", which claims more
42	than `-1` shows. Comparing against a run with the real code would settle it, and that has not been done.
43	
44	## The same bugs with the printer in LAN mode, real printer, 2026-11-01 about 18:46 to 19:00
45	
46	Kenneth turned on LAN Only, and the P1S announced `DevConnect.bambu.com: lan` and `DevBind.bambu.com: free`. Same method
47	as the run below: real plug-in, real panel, a script instead of a model. The script stops at the app's access code
48	request, so nothing was sent to the printer by the app. One slip of mine: a status check pinged the printer twice, with
49	no reply.
50	
51	Code from before the fixes (`69780c7af4`):
52	
53	```
54	app has heard, at 0 s: nothing
55	printer_connect {"deviceId":"192.168.0.198"} -> "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now; check again with printer_connection_status."
56	printer_connection_status {} -> candidates: []
57	app has heard, at 5 s: P1s id=01P00C652900116 at 192.168.0.198 connection=lan bind=free

## Wrong access code and the same printer saved twice, real P1S, 2026-11-02 04:58 to 05:23

Real P1S at 192.168.0.198 in LAN mode (`lan`, `free`, firmware 01.10.00.00), real plug-in 02.03.00.62, real panel, a
temporary script instead of a model. Before is `ff10faa501`; after is `788ff792b7`. One attempt per version with the
deliberately wrong code `WRONG123`. A temporary line printed the plug-in's answer, because the app log does not.

Entry B of the same model, unlinked, with entry A linked by writing the serial into the link record:

```
before: printer_connection_status -> candidates: [], seen: []
before: note: The network search has listened for 15 seconds and has found no printer of this model.
before: printer_connect -> The network search has listened for 25 seconds and has found no printer of this model in LAN mode.
after:  printer_connection_status -> seen: [{"address":"192.168.0.198","detail":"Bambu Lab P1S","name":"P1s","reason":"linked_elsewhere"}]
after:  printer_connect -> P1s at 192.168.0.198 was seen on the network, but it is already the printer "Bambu Lab P1S" in this app, and a device connects to one saved printer. It cannot be connected as it is.
```

Wrong code on entry A:

```
both:   plug-in answered: state=1 (failed) msg=-1
both:   a modal dialog appeared; the script closed it. In this path its text is "Connect P1s failed! [SN:..., code=-1]"
both:   saved access code after the attempt: in memory present, in app config present
before: Connection to Bambu Lab P1S failed: The selected printer changed. Select this printer again to reconnect.
after:  Connection to Bambu Lab P1S failed: The printer refused the connection; Bambu's network plug-in reported code -1. Check that the printer is on and in LAN mode, then try again.
```

What did not match the assumptions:

- The plug-in said `-1`, not `5`. `5` has never been seen on real hardware.
- The before text was "The selected printer changed", not "The printer is no longer available".
- The wrong code was not erased, because the erase runs only on `5`. The code from the attempt stayed saved.
- The app log has no line with the code. The plug-in's own log is encrypted (`debug_network_*.log.enc`).

Not known: whether `-1` means the printer refused the code. The app log shows 22 seconds between selecting the printer
(05:22:46.16) and the failure clearing it (05:23:08.25). My guess is that this is a timeout and not a refusal, but nothing
confirms it. TCP 8883 and 990 accepted connections from the same Mac. The after text says "refused", which claims more
than `-1` shows. Comparing against a run with the real code would settle it, and that has not been done.

printer_connection_status {} -> {...,"search":{"secondsAgo":120,"state":"port_taken"},"seen":[],"state":"not_configured"}
```

Port let go right after that note (`HARNESS RESULT FAIL failures=2`), `lsof -nP -iUDP:2021` empty from then on:

```
note at 20 s: The network search cannot hear printers: this app is not listening on UDP port 2021, where they announce themselves, so none can be found, whatever mode they are in. It takes that port only as it starts, so searching needs this app restarted.
printer_connection_status {} -> {...,"search":{"secondsAgo":120,"state":"not_listening"},"seen":[],"state":"not_configured"}
```

Port free (`HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0`): the printer was found at 14 s, no port note, all refusals as above.

Why a restart and not a recovery: after the holder let go, the port stayed empty for the 80 seconds watched with each of
these: stopping and starting discovery; the same with a 3-second wait; the same with the "sending" flag and a 1-second
wait; and `hot_reload_network_plugin()`, which returned true. Starting the app with the port free does bind it.

What is not tested: only another JusPrin and a Python script held the port, not Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer. Windows
makes no claim (`discovery_port()` returns `Ours`); whether a held port hides printers there is unknown. The Linux code
path has not been run. Port tests in `agent_bridge_tests` use a fake; the socket check itself is covered only by these
live runs.

## A correction

Earlier this note said the printer was off, from its TCP port 8883 timing out and no recent line in the app log. That
was inference and is not reliable: at 07:30 port 8883 timed out while the printer was announcing on UDP.

## Command, to repeat it

```bash
cd /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/festive-lederberg-693438
F=/tmp/claude/netcheck; rm -rf "$F"; mkdir -p "$F"
cp -R "$HOME/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/plugins" "$F/plugins"
build/arm64/tests/shell/Release/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness --printer-network-check "$F" 192.168.0.198 02.03.00.62 2>&1 | grep -aE "HARNESS (NETWORK|RESULT)|network_check.*FAIL"
```

## Why the harness is not the one the task named

`probe.call` cannot reach these tools. McpServer.cpp refuses them with "This tool is not exposed by JusPrin MCP.",
because they have only `ToolExposure::Printer`. So the commit adds `--printer-network-check`: no model, the real
plug-in, the real `OrcaPrinterBackend`, and a scripted stand-in for the model.

## Real plug-in, printer not heard (`HARNESS RESULT FAIL failures=2`)

The two failures are the checks that need the printer. This is the timeout path, which the 07:30 run did not reach.
Quoted from the run:

```
printer_connect {"deviceId":"192.168.0.198"} -> {"error":{"code":"unknown_device","message":"No network search has run yet in this conversation; printer_connection_status starts it."}}
printer_connection_status {} -> {"address":"","candidates":[],"hostType":"","message":"","nozzleMismatch":false,"provider":"bambu","search":{"secondsAgo":0,"state":"started"},"seen":[],"state":"not_configured"}
printer_connect {"deviceId":"192.168.0.198"} -> {"error":{"code":"unknown_device","message":"The network search started 0 seconds ago and has found no printer of this model yet. The app posts a note when one appears, or after about 15 seconds with none."}}
note at 15 s: The network search has listened for 15 seconds and has found no printer of this model. The app posts another note if one appears.
printer_connection_status {} -> {"address":"","candidates":[],"hostType":"","message":"","nozzleMismatch":false,"provider":"bambu","search":{"secondsAgo":120,"state":"listening"},"seen":[],"state":"not_configured"}
```

## Simulated announcement (`HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0`)

**No printer was involved.** With `--simulate-announce`, 25 seconds in, the harness hands
`DeviceManager::on_machine_alive` the announcement recorded in the 2026-10-31 log. This tests everything after the
plug-in, including `OrcaPrinterBackend::connection`, and not the plug-in itself. After the same first three lines:

```
note at 15 s: The network search has listened for 15 seconds and has found no printer of this model. The app posts another note if one appears.
simulated announcement, no printer involved
note at 25 s: The network search found P1s at 192.168.0.198 with LAN Only off, which cannot be connected as it is. Connecting it is the person's choice, and the printer prepares prints without a connection.
printer_connection_status {} -> {"address":"","candidates":[],"hostType":"","message":"","nozzleMismatch":false,"provider":"bambu","search":{"secondsAgo":25,"state":"listening"},"seen":[{"address":"192.168.0.198","name":"P1s","reason":"cloud_mode"}],"state":"not_configured"}
printer_connect {"deviceId":"192.168.0.198"} -> {"error":{"code":"unknown_device","message":"P1s at 192.168.0.198 was seen on the network with LAN Only off. It cannot be connected as it is. Connecting it is the person's choice, and the printer prepares prints without a connection."}}
printer_connect {"deviceId":"P1s"} -> the same refusal
printer_connect {"address":"192.168.0.198","hostType":"moonraker"} -> the same refusal
```

## Tests

- Before the fix: `[printer-conversation]` had 7 of 67 test cases failing, 46 assertions, with the old sentence
  "No printer in LAN mode is on the network now" and `key 'seen' not found` / `key 'search' not found`.
- After the fix: `agent_bridge_tests` all pass, 20014 assertions in 497 test cases; with the port work, 20126 in 499.
- The port tests failed first: 24 assertions before detection existed, and 2 test cases when the restart was still in.
- The two tests that passed or did not exist before the fix were proven by removing that part of it: without the
  reset on Undo, and without the "already reached" rule, 2 test cases fail.
- `npm test` in AgentUI: 624 passed, again with the port work.
- Shell harness `--printer-setup`, which uses the fake printer: `HARNESS RESULT PASS failures=0`, 252 checks, again
  with the port work.
- `tests/printer_prompt/test_responses.py`: 8 of 9 pass. `test_the_unrun_result_is_the_apps_own` fails on a lookup
  unrelated to this change: it searches OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp for text now in ProviderAgent.cpp. Not fixed here.
- No live-model prompt was run.

## Choices to look at

1. `CLOUD01` in the test fixture has no address, and in the app such a printer comes from the Bambu account list,
   which holds printers wherever they are. Saying it "is on the network with LAN Only off" would be a guess, so it
   gets its own reason, `account_only`, and the wording says it has not been seen on the network. This goes past the
   brief, which named only cloud mode.
2. `ConnectionCandidate` gained `account_only`, set in `OrcaPrinterBackend::connection`, for that reason.
3. The sentence "None listed means LAN mode is off..." moved from `printerInstructions.ts` to the
   `printer_connection_status` description, and now applies only once the search is `listening`. The brief did not
   name that file, but the sentence contradicted the search state and is a rule about one tool. Not measured with a
   model; `connect-bambu-not-found` in the prompt tests is the case to watch.
4. After the 15-second note the app keeps looking, every 5 seconds, until a printer appears: the P1S first answered
   38 seconds in. `saved_printers()` runs on each look, on the GUI thread, for as long as the chat stays open. Its
   cost was not measured.
5. If someone says "never mind" right after a status check, the 15-second note still starts a turn, so the model
   speaks once more. Nothing tells the app they lost interest.

184	# How printers announce: what is known, 2026-11-01
185	
186	Withdrawn: my suggestion to wait 45 seconds. It rested on six timings and no search.
187	
188	Official: Bambu's wiki lists device discovery on UDP 1990 and 2021, SSDP multicast or broadcast, in cloud and LAN mode. Seen only through a search result; fetching the page returned HTTP 402. I found no published timing.
189	
190	Community, not official: one person captured a P1S in LAN mode sending every 5 seconds, destination toggling between 1990 and 2021, which would make 2021 every 10 seconds. One capture, on another network.
191	
192	General: IETF documents say Wi-Fi multicast has no acknowledgement or retransmission. That packet loss causes our delays is a hypothesis, not tested.
193	
194	Measured here: two announcements 9.9 s apart in a 30 s listen, first at 19.2 s. App first-heard times 14, 21, 25, 25, 40 s, plus 38 s on 2026-10-31, and one 120 s miss. A 10 s period does not explain those, so something else is at work; unknown what.
195	
196	Void: a 10-minute listen from about 10:37 heard nothing because the Mac had moved to 192.168.15.221 after a clamshell sleep at 10:14. The 08:57 miss predates that sleep and stays unexplained.
197	
198	Not measured yet: announcement gaps over a long listen; first-heard times over many no-model runs. Both are free and need the Mac on 192.168.0.x.
199	
200	# Faster sources than trial and error, 2026-11-01
201	
202	- Kenneth's app log `debug_Sat_Oct_31_07_19_33_85053.log.0`: 1,195 on_machine_alive lines for the P1S, 18:23 to 23:07 on 2026-10-31. Gaps round to 10 s (1,007), 20 s (155), 30 s (26), 40 s (4), 50 s (1), plus one of 2,783 s. These lines are written only when a field changes, so a long gap is not evidence of a lost packet; the 10 s steps are evidence of the period at which the app hears the printer.
203	- ClusterM/open-bamboo-networking `research/06.01-ssdp.md`: NOTIFY on UDP 2021, about every 5 s on one P2S capture, 1990 only as a Host header. `research/08.04-lan.md`: `start_discovery`'s `sending` = also send M-SEARCH, and Studio passes false, as JusPrin does. Community reverse engineering; other models; disagrees in details with the P1S gist.
204	- maziggy/bambuddy `backend/app/services/discovery.py`: sends M-SEARCH every 3 s to trigger responses while listening on 2021. Whether a P1S answers M-SEARCH is not shown.
205	- `strings` on the plug-in: socket threads for 1990 and 2021, a broadcast thread, and M-SEARCH text.
206	
207	Open lead, untested: the app listens passively; asking with M-SEARCH may shorten the wait and make the timing question matter less.
208	Next test: packet capture beside one no-model run separates "never reached the Mac" from "reached the Mac but the app did not hear it".

# How printers announce: what is known, 2026-11-01

Withdrawn: my suggestion to wait 45 seconds. It rested on six timings and no search.

Official: Bambu's wiki lists device discovery on UDP 1990 and 2021, SSDP multicast or broadcast, in cloud and LAN mode. Seen only through a search result; fetching the page returned HTTP 402. I found no published timing.

Community, not official: one person captured a P1S in LAN mode sending every 5 seconds, destination toggling between 1990 and 2021, which would make 2021 every 10 seconds. One capture, on another network.

General: IETF documents say Wi-Fi multicast has no acknowledgement or retransmission. That packet loss causes our delays is a hypothesis, not tested.

Measured here: two announcements 9.9 s apart in a 30 s listen, first at 19.2 s. App first-heard times 14, 21, 25, 25, 40 s, plus 38 s on 2026-10-31, and one 120 s miss. A 10 s period does not explain those, so something else is at work; unknown what.

Void: a 10-minute listen from about 10:37 heard nothing because the Mac had moved to 192.168.15.221 after a clamshell sleep at 10:14. The 08:57 miss predates that sleep and stays unexplained.

Not measured yet: announcement gaps over a long listen; first-heard times over many no-model runs. Both are free and need the Mac on 192.168.0.x.

# Faster sources than trial and error, 2026-11-01

- Kenneth's app log `debug_Sat_Oct_31_07_19_33_85053.log.0`: 1,195 on_machine_alive lines for the P1S, 18:23 to 23:07 on 2026-10-31. Gaps round to 10 s (1,007), 20 s (155), 30 s (26), 40 s (4), 50 s (1), plus one of 2,783 s. These lines are written only when a field changes, so a long gap is not evidence of a lost packet; the 10 s steps are evidence of the period at which the app hears the printer.
- ClusterM/open-bamboo-networking `research/06.01-ssdp.md`: NOTIFY on UDP 2021, about every 5 s on one P2S capture, 1990 only as a Host header. `research/08.04-lan.md`: `start_discovery`'s `sending` = also send M-SEARCH, and Studio passes false, as JusPrin does. Community reverse engineering; other models; disagrees in details with the P1S gist.
- maziggy/bambuddy `backend/app/services/discovery.py`: sends M-SEARCH every 3 s to trigger responses while listening on 2021. Whether a P1S answers M-SEARCH is not shown.
- `strings` on the plug-in: socket threads for 1990 and 2021, a broadcast thread, and M-SEARCH text.

Open lead, untested: the app listens passively; asking with M-SEARCH may shorten the wait and make the timing question matter less.
Next test: packet capture beside one no-model run separates "never reached the Mac" from "reached the Mac but the app did not hear it".

184	# How printers announce: what is known, 2026-11-01
185	
186	Withdrawn: my suggestion to wait 45 seconds. It rested on six timings and no search.
187	
188	Official: Bambu's wiki lists device discovery on UDP 1990 and 2021, SSDP multicast or broadcast, in cloud and LAN mode. Seen only through a search result; fetching the page returned HTTP 402. I found no published timing.
189	
190	Community, not official: one person captured a P1S in LAN mode sending every 5 seconds, destination toggling between 1990 and 2021, which would make 2021 every 10 seconds. One capture, on another network.
191	
192	General: IETF documents say Wi-Fi multicast has no acknowledgement or retransmission. That packet loss causes our delays is a hypothesis, not tested.
193	
194	Measured here: two announcements 9.9 s apart in a 30 s listen, first at 19.2 s. App first-heard times 14, 21, 25, 25, 40 s, plus 38 s on 2026-10-31, and one 120 s miss. A 10 s period does not explain those, so something else is at work; unknown what.
195	
196	Void: a 10-minute listen from about 10:37 heard nothing because the Mac had moved to 192.168.15.221 after a clamshell sleep at 10:14. The 08:57 miss predates that sleep and stays unexplained.
197	
198	Not measured yet: announcement gaps over a long listen; first-heard times over many no-model runs. Both are free and need the Mac on 192.168.0.x.

Gaps round to 10 s (1,007), 20 s (155), 30 s (26), 40 s (4), 50 s (1), plus one of 2,783 s. Community reverse engineering; other models; disagrees in details with the P1S gist.
204	- maziggy/bambuddy `backend/app/services/discovery.py`: sends M-SEARCH every 3 s to trigger responses while listening on 2021. Whether a P1S answers M-SEARCH is not shown.

11	On 2026-10-21 Kenneth's Mac ran at load average 32 on 12 cores for over an hour. The cause was one Claude session (the "Show MCP edits without an agent" worktree session) that launched four `nohup cmake --build … --config Release` runs between 10:56 and 11:05 into the same build dir (`.claude/worktrees/mcp-external-edits/build/arm64`), three with identical target sets. 2026-10-24 (import-behavior work, PR TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin#38): adding EmptyPlateHint.cpp to `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake` after committing made the next build re-run CMake. The configure step reads the git hash into `-DGIT_COMMIT_HASH=\"<sha>\"`, which is on every TU's command line, so the whole tree (libslic3r included) recompiled at -j4: roughly an hour.

Not the only cause of that symptom: if the build log starts with "premature end of file; recovering", see [[ninja-deps-bad-record-repeat-rebuild]].

**Why:** a command-line change invalidates every object in ninja's log, not just the touched target.
**How to apply:** add new source files to `sources.cmake` before the first build of a worktree, and avoid committing between a cmake-file edit and the build that needs it. Related: [[jusprin-worktree-build]], [[pkill-cmake-build-leaves-ninja]].

Also learned that day: OrcaSlicer reinstalls its own `PlaterDropTarget` after every slice completes (`Plater::priv::on_process_completed`, `is_finished` is true for every non-slice-all run), so any fork-owned Plater drop target must be put back afterwards (the shell does it on idle).

import { loadSkills } from './skillParser';
export { loadSkills, parseSkill, type Skill } from './skillParser';

// Every skills/<name>/SKILL.md, bundled with the page and sent to the app
// once per connection with the skills message.
const skillFiles = import.meta.glob('./skills/*/SKILL.md', {
  query: '?raw',
  import: 'default',
  eager: true,
}) as Record<string, string>;

export const skills = loadSkills(skillFiles);
// A project skill is text for one kind of situation. The page writes each one
// as skills/<name>/SKILL.md: YAML frontmatter, then the body, which is the
// text the model gets. A skill with a `trigger` is added by the app to one
// request when the event it names happens; the model does not choose it. A
// skill with a `description` is listed for the model, which reads it with
// skill_read when the description fits. A skill may have both.
export interface Skill {
  name: string;
  trigger?: string;
  description?: string;

        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!

using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers

```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Test Suite Organization

### libslic3r Tests
Core slicing engine tests covering:
- **Geometry operations**: Points, polygons, lines, Voronoi diagrams
- **File formats**: STL, 3MF, AMF parsing and validation
- **Algorithms**: Clipper operations, mesh boolean operations, optimization
- **Configuration**: Print settings validation and parsing
- **Utilities**: String processing, time utilities, data structures

### fff_print Tests
Fused Filament Fabrication specific tests:
- **G-code generation**: Writer functionality, cooling, lift/unlift
- **Slicing algorithms**: Layer generation, infill patterns
- **Print mechanics**: Flow calculations, extrusion, support material
- **Model processing**: Print objects, skirt/brim generation

### sla_print Tests
Stereolithography specific tests:
- **SLA print processing**: Layer curing, support generation
- **Raycast operations**: Light path calculations
- **Test utilities**: SLA-specific helper functions

## Writing New Tests - Best Practices

### File Organization
1. **Naming Convention**: `test_<feature>.cpp` (e.g., `test_geometry.cpp`)
2. **Header Structure**: Include `<catch2/catch_all.hpp>` first, then relevant headers
3. **Namespace Usage**: Use `using namespace Slic3r;` for convenience
4. **File Placement**: Add to appropriate test directory and update CMakeLists.txt

### Test Naming and Structure
```cpp
#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>
#include "libslic3r/Point.hpp"

using namespace Slic3r;

TEST_CASE("Feature description", "[category_tag]") {
    // Test implementation
}
```

### Tagging System
Use descriptive tags for test categorization:
- `[Geometry]` - Geometric operations and calculations
- `[GCodeWriter]` - G-code generation functionality  
- `[Config]` - Configuration and settings tests
- `[FileFormat]` - File I/O operations (STL, 3MF, etc.)
- `[Algorithm]` - Core algorithms and processing
- `[Performance]` - Performance benchmarks (if applicable)

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)
REQUIRE_THROWS_MATCHES(function_call(), SpecificException, 
                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers
REQUIRE_THAT(value, WithinRel(expected, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));
```

### Sections for Test Organization

TEST_CASE("Complex feature testing", "[Feature]") {

### BDD-Style Tests
Use for complex scenarios and user story testing:

> **Note**: BDD macros are aliases for TEST_CASE and SECTION with prefixed names
```cpp
SCENARIO("User performs complex operation", "[UserStory]") {
    GIVEN("A specific setup condition") {

            auto result = writer.some_operation();
            
            THEN("Expected outcome occurs") {
                REQUIRE(result.size() > 0);
                
                AND_WHEN("Follow-up action occurs") {

}

### Test Fixtures

public:

// Template fixtures for type-parameterized tests

public:

### Advanced Testing Features

#### Logging and Information Macros
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Advanced logging", "[Logging]") {
    INFO("This info persists until end of scope");
    
    SECTION("Section A") {
        INFO("Section A specific info");
        CAPTURE(some_variable, another_var);  // Captures variable names and values

    }

}

### Custom String Conversions

#### For Custom Types
```cpp
// Method 1: operator<< overload (preferred)
std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const Point& point) {
    os << "Point(" << point.x << ", " << point.y << ")";
    return os;
}

// Method 2: StringMaker specialization

    template<>

// Method 4: Exception translation

}

// Method 5: Disable range iteration for problematic types

## Running and Debugging Tests

### Building Tests
```bash
# Build all tests
cd build && make

# Build specific test suite
cd build && make libslic3r_tests

# Build and run tests
cd build && make && ctest
```

### Running Tests

#### Essential Test Execution Patterns
```bash
# REQUIRED: Random order with assertion warnings (best practice)
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# Run all tests with verbose output via CTest
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure

# Run specific test suite with best practices
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# Filter tests with specific tags
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "[Geometry]" --order rand

# Filter by test name patterns

# Exclude tests (negation)

# Combine filters: (Geometry AND Config) OR Algorithm
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests "[Geometry][Config],[Algorithm]" --order rand

# List available tests, tags, and reporters
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-tests
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-tags  
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --list-reporters

# Debug failing tests

cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --success  # Show passing tests too
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --durations yes  # Show timing info

# Abort on first failure
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --abort

# Test sharding for parallel execution (MUST share random seed)

cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &
cd build && ./tests/libslic3r/libslic3r_tests --order rand --shard-index 3 --shard-count 4 --rng-seed 0xBEEF &

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

### Runtime Performance
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Performance-sensitive test", "[Performance]") {
    // Manual timing example (Catch2's built-in BENCHMARK macro is also available)
    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    
    auto result = expensive_operation();
    
    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);
    
    REQUIRE(result.is_valid());
    REQUIRE(duration.count() < 1000);  // Should complete in < 1 second
    
    INFO("Operation took " << duration.count() << "ms");
}
```

## Integration with CMake

### Adding New Test Files
1. Create test file: `test_new_feature.cpp`
2. Add to appropriate `CMakeLists.txt`:
```cmake
add_executable(${_TEST_NAME}_tests 
    ${_TEST_NAME}_tests.cpp
    test_existing_feature.cpp

### Advanced Test Discovery
```cmake
# Basic test discovery
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: ")

# Advanced test discovery with customization
catch_discover_tests(${_TEST_NAME}_tests
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}: "
    TEST_SUFFIX " (auto)"
    WORKING_DIRECTORY ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}
    EXTRA_ARGS --order rand --warn NoAssertions
    PROPERTIES 
        TIMEOUT 300
        LABELS "unit;core"

    REPORTER junit
    OUTPUT_DIR ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/test-results
    OUTPUT_PREFIX "results_"
    OUTPUT_SUFFIX ".xml"
)

    SHARD_COUNT 4
    TEST_PREFIX "${_TEST_NAME}_shard: "
)
```

### Conditional Test Compilation
```cmake
# Feature-dependent tests
if (TARGET OpenVDB::openvdb)

## Known Issues and Workarounds

### Platform-Specific Issues
```cpp
// MinGW/CygWin slow linking workaround
// Use: -fuse-ld=lld flag to speed up linking significantly

// Visual Studio 2017 raw string literal bug
#define CATCH_CONFIG_DISABLE_STRINGIFICATION
// This disables expression stringification but works around the compiler bug

// Visual Studio 2022 spaceship operator issue
// REQUIRE((a <=> b) == 0);  // May not compile with MSVC
// Workaround: use clang-cl or avoid spaceship in assertions

// QNX/VxWorks C stdlib issues
#include <cfoo>           // Use C++ headers
std::foo_function();     // Always call qualified
// NOT: #include <foo.h> and foo_function();
```

### Catch2 v3 Features Available
```cpp
// OrcaSlicer is on Catch2 v3.11.0 - all of these ARE available:
// SKIP() macro                           - v3.3.0+
// Opt-in thread-safe assertions          - v3.9.0+ (NOT enabled here; see Thread Safety)
// Built-in BENCHMARK / BENCHMARK_ADVANCED - v3.x
// testCasePartial events                 - v3.0.1+
// Multiple reporters simultaneously      - v3.0.1+
// STATIC_CHECK macro                     - v3.0.1+
// Built-in test sharding (--shard-*)     - v3.x

### Test Organization Best Practices

#### Project Structure Rules
1. **1:1 correspondence**: One test binary per library/module
2. **Hidden tests**: Use `[.]` or `[!benchmark]` tags for tests that shouldn't run by default
3. **Tag hierarchy**: Use consistent tagging scheme across the project
4. **File naming**: Follow `test_<feature>.cpp` pattern

```bash

# For coverage analysis
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions --reporter console --success

# For performance tracking

# Connecting a Bambu Lab printer

The rules above still apply. The person is trying to connect this printer. This says what each state the tools report means here, and the one next step for it. The app's notes report the same states in words, so a note is read by the same line. Read `printer_connection_status` first if nothing has been read yet, and again whenever the person says something changed: a read is how you learn what the app knows now.

## What the search has heard

- `started`, with `candidates` and `seen` empty: the search has only just begun, so nothing is known about the printer yet. Say you are looking, and end your message. The app posts a note when a printer appears, or after about 15 seconds with none, and starts your next turn; reading the status again before then shows nothing new.
- `listening`, with `candidates` and `seen` empty: nothing has been heard so far, and the search goes on after this. On a real P1S the first announcement took between 8 and 40 seconds, so this is silence, not a finding: never say the printer is not on the network, is off, or is in the wrong mode. Say nothing has been heard yet and that you are still listening, ask what the printer's own screen shows about its connection, and wait for their answer or the app's next note.
- `port_taken`: another app on this computer holds the port printers announce on, so nothing can be heard, whatever the printer is doing. Do not ask about the printer. Ask them to close that other app, which may be another slicer, and then restart this app.
- `not_listening`: this app is not listening and takes the port only as it starts. Do not ask about the printer. Ask them to restart this app.

## A printer it heard

- `candidates`, with one printer: it is in LAN mode and can be connected. If they have asked to connect, call `printer_connect` with its `deviceId` without asking again. With more than one, ask which, one choice each.
- `credential_requested`: the form is up. Say in one sentence to type the access code shown on the printer into that form, then wait: the app checks the printer and its note says how it went.
- `cloud_mode`: this printer is on the network with LAN Only off, and it cannot be connected until LAN Only is on. Say that, with its address. Turning it on is their choice, and they can prepare prints for it either way. It is set on the printer's screen; you do not know what the menus are called on this model, so ask what they see rather than naming a path. When they say it is on, read `printer_connection_status` again.
- `linked_elsewhere`: this device is already the saved printer named in `detail`, and a device connects to one saved printer. Say so. The next step is connecting that printer, from Connect… in its menu on Home, not this one.

## When something stops it

- `failed`: the app's note gives the reason; say it in one sentence and add no cause of your own. The plug-in's code -1 does not tell a wrong access code from no answer, so never say which it was. Ask them to compare the access code on the printer's screen with what they typed; when they want to try again, call `printer_connect` again, which opens the form.
- `unknown_device`: `printer_connect` refused the name it was given, and the message says why. When it says no search has run, call `printer_connection_status`. Otherwise follow the line above for what it names.
- `unavailable`: the status's `message` says why it cannot connect. When that is Bambu's network plug-in, the app shows the person a notice with an Install button under the message: tell them to use it, and wait for the app's note that it is installed before reading the status again.

## Anything else

A state or reason this does not list is real and unexplained: say what the tool's words say, add no cause, ask what they see on the printer, and wait. Name no menu, screen or setting you did not read from a tool or from the person. Whenever they would rather leave it, they can: it is optional.

193:## Writing UI code
194-
195-Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
196-exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
197-from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
198-only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.
199-
200-1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
201-   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
202-   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
203-   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
204-   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
205-   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
206-   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
207-   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
208-   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
209-2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
210-   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
211-   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
212-   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
213-   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
214-   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
215-   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
